What-if values appear separately and never in the valid budget.
A concentration needs a volume to become an amount.
A matched blank over 60 min cannot be compared with 120 min without a model.
10 nmol over 60 min → 20 nmol over 120 min under a stated linear model.
Exposure 60 min vs collection 120 min.

A nondetect is [0, LOD]; its lower bound 0 lies within any budget.
A nondetect without its limit cannot be bounded.
Dropping the system blank leaves the electrolyte unbounded.
Budget = gas + system blank (22.45), not gas + blank + membrane (37.45).
Overlapping measurements are not summed without a selected coverage model.
Unknown sources can only enlarge the budget, so 'not excluded' is robust.
A single-species bound leaves NOx unknown, so the result stays inconclusive.
ppm is ambiguous for a liquid-phase product.
A standardized unit with an actual basis is contradictory.
Cell temperature must not be applied to a standardized volume.
sccm uses 273.15 K reference, not the 323.15 K gas temperature.
Bounding one feed says nothing about another; the unmeasured feed stays unknown.
Supplier purity does not establish a measured delivered-gas concentration.
6 L at 298.15 K and 1 atm gives the same budget as 50 mL/min × 120 min.

Upstream measurement is a what-if, not a delivered bound.
Reference gas calculation (≈245 nmol) covers a 190–210 nmol observation.
Tightened impurity bound (≈2.45 nmol) is below the observation.
Missing gas measurement must be unknown, not zero.
